record.paper_title: Bimagic Squares of Bimagic Squares and an Open Problem
record.context_brief: Bimagic-sum invariance in nested square constructions
record.original_question: For the three tabulated families of bimagic squares — order 256×256 with listed subgroups 64×64, 16×16, and 4×4; order 625×625 with listed subgroups 125×125, 25×25, and 5×5; and order 2401×2401 with listed subgroups 343×343, 49×49, and 7×7 — prove mathematically the observed property stated by the source: for k = 4, 5, and 7, in the first sub-group the bimagic sum S2 is the same, summarized by the pattern k^4 → k^3 → k^2 → k^1.

evidence.quote: For more details see the table given at the end as an open problem to prove it mathematically.
We observe from the above table that in the first sub-group in each case the S2 is same, i.e., k^4 → k^3 → k^2 → k^1, k = 4, 5 and 7. Now the question is to prove it mathematically?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A bimagic square of order n is an n×n array filled with positive integers such that every row, every column, and both main diagonals have the same sum S₁ (the magic sum), and such that the array obtained by replacing each entry by its square is again a magic square; the common sum of squares in rows, columns, and diagonals is denoted S₂ and called the bimagic sum.

Consider the following nested constructions. For each prime power base k ∈ {4, 5, 7}, form a bimagic square of order k⁴ × k⁴ whose entries are the integers 1, 2, …, k⁸. Suppose this square admits a hierarchy of "sub-group" partitions: the k⁴ × k⁴ square is partitioned into k² × k² blocks of size k³ × k³ (the first sub-group), each k³ × k³ block is partitioned into k² × k² blocks of size k × k (here viewed at scale k², k¹), giving a nested sequence of orders

   k⁴ → k³ → k² → k¹.

Concretely the three families considered are:
 • k = 4: orders 256 → 64 → 16 → 4,
 • k = 5: orders 625 → 125 → 25 → 5,
 • k = 7: orders 2401 → 343 → 49 → 7.

Empirically, in each of these three families one observes that the bimagic sum S₂ taken over each k³ × k³ sub-block of the first sub-group is the same constant (independent of which sub-block of order k³ is chosen).

Prove rigorously that for k ∈ {4, 5, 7} (and in the general scheme k⁴ → k³ → k² → k¹), every k³ × k³ sub-block of the first sub-group of the bimagic square of order k⁴ has the same bimagic sum S₂. Equivalently, identify the structural property of the construction that forces this invariance and give a mathematical proof.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for the specific invariance property k⁴ → k³ → k² → k¹ of bimagic sums in nested bimagic squares of orders 256, 625, and 2401 did not return any published proof or refutation. General literature on bimagic squares (Wikipedia, MathWorld, recent papers on existence of normal bimagic squares of even order) does not address this particular sub-block invariance claim, so the status appears unresolved in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Multimagic square - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A bimagic square is a magic square that remains magic when all of its numbers are replaced by their squares.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background definition of bimagic square but does not address the specific nested invariance problem.

status_evidence.title: Bimagic Square -- from Wolfram MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: Reference page on bimagic squares with constructions and constants.
status_evidence.claim: No mention of the k^4 → k^3 → k^2 → k^1 sub-block invariance result.

status_evidence.title: A complete solution to the existence of normal bimagic squares of even order
status_evidence.snippet: Settles existence of normal bimagic squares of even order.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature focuses on existence rather than the nested sub-block invariance question, providing no resolution of it.
